items.stem: A line must build 480 vehicles in an 8-hour shift with no breaks. What is the approximate takt time?

options.rationale: This ignores that there are 28,800 seconds in the shift for 480 units.
Takt = available time / demand = 28,800 s / 480 = 60 s per vehicle.
This confuses demand count with time per unit.
That is the whole shift, not the per-unit pace.

items.explanation: Takt = available time / demand = 28,800 s / 480 = 60 s per vehicle.

items.stem: In the Toyota Production System, what does 'jidoka' (autonomation) primarily refer to?

options.text: Running every machine at maximum speed regardless of defects
options.rationale: That contradicts the quality focus of jidoka.

options.text: Giving machines and operators the ability to stop production automatically when an abnormality is detected
options.rationale: Jidoka builds in the ability to halt when a defect or problem occurs, so quality issues are not passed downstream.

options.text: Holding large buffer inventories between stations
options.rationale: That is the opposite of lean inventory practice.

options.text: Eliminating all human workers from the plant
options.rationale: Jidoka is about human-machine quality cooperation, not removing people.

items.explanation: Jidoka builds in the ability to halt when a defect or problem occurs, so quality issues are not passed downstream.

items.stem: A continuous-improvement team wants to reduce waste on an assembly line. Select TWO activities that lean production classifies as waste (muda) to be reduced.

options.text: Overproduction of parts ahead of demand
options.rationale: Overproduction is the foremost of the seven wastes in lean thinking.

options.text: Operators waiting for parts that have not arrived
options.rationale: Waiting is a recognised form of waste that adds no value.

options.text: Value-adding assembly operations the customer pays for
options.rationale: Value-adding work is not waste; it is the purpose of the line.

options.text: Standardised work that stabilises the process
options.rationale: Standardised work is a lean enabler, not a waste.

options.text: Scheduled preventive maintenance that avoids breakdowns
options.rationale: Planned maintenance reduces losses rather than being waste itself.

items.explanation: Overproduction is the foremost of the seven wastes in lean thinking.
